Royal Marine Andy Gatrick, who was 18 at the time, came across two injured Argentine soldiers during the Battle of Mount Harriet in 1982. The helmet belonging to one of the men, both of whom were captured by the Marines, had a name on it: Hector. Gatrick, now 63, managed to track him down and flew back on 23 October to return it. He was joined by Mick Dawson, another Royal Marine veteran from Rottingdean, East Sussex, who filmed the exchange for a new documentary called Hector's Helmet. Image source, Andy Gatrick Image caption, Royal Marine veteran Andy Gatrick, left, has returned a helmet he took during the Battle of Mount Harriet "In a very emotional day, he handed the helmet back in person to the guy he could have just as easily killed that night," said Dawson, from Rottingdean in East Sussex. Dawson, 62, told BBC Radio Sussex : "Long story short, our kit was rubbish, we had rubbish helmets that you couldn't wear. We were in berets. "They had good kit, American helmets. He borrowed one of their helmets which belonged to Hector." The two met metres from each other during the Battle of Mount Harriet, which took place on 11 and 12 June, 1982. Gatrick, from Bolton, Greater Manchester, said in footage sent to the BBC: "I put my weapon down and as I bent down to put the strap over my shoulders, I saw movement and a cloth which looked like a white handkerchief. The high street of bygone Marple has been subsumed by a score of flourishing independents. A greasy spoon once plainly boasting “Hot And Cold Sandwiches” has beco And the biggest change is still to come. In December, the town will unveil its £20m Marple Hub: a sustainable red-brick, glazed complex with a new library, a five-lane swimming pool, a gym, a clinic and a cafe. Rochdale firm, Winterburns, is set to take over security immediately, with a beefed up, 24-hour presence on site. The firm will also start clearing the mountain of debris which has built up over years of neglect, includin Teams will soon start the delicate internal strip out of Warwick Mill and London House. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
